introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography (0750), Paper 3, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2019. Duration: three and a quarter hours.**

Answer FOUR questions in all. Answer question ONE and three others, choosing ONE question from SECTION B and TWO from SECTION C. Question ONE carries thirty-one marks and the rest carry twenty-three marks each.

Only the required number of questions will be marked.

In answering questions on this paper, you are encouraged to refer to your own field and practical work where relevant. Credit will be awarded for such references.

Candidates are advised NOT to attempt the questions on field investigations if such an exercise has not been carried out.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Calculators are allowed.

Materials required: Topographic map, Graph Paper and two outline maps of Cameroon.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - FIELD WORK AND TECHNIQUES**

2. Based on field work which you carried out in physical or human Geography, choose one of the following six topics:

(i) Rock and relief,

(ii) Stream channel flow characteristics,

(iii) Vegetation characteristics,

(iv) Traffic flow characteristics,

(v) Rural or urban land use/characteristics:

(vi) A modern farm or cottage industry

Les questions 2 et 3 sont rangées en SECTION B (l'en-tête « FIELD WORK AND TECHNIQUES » précède la question 2 et la question 3 suit sans nouvel en-tête) ; les questions 4 à 7 en SECTION C (« CAMEROON »).

Question 2 : question à choisir parmi six thèmes de travail de terrain (« Based on field work which you carried out »). Les corrigés sont un plan de réponse complet, détaillé pour le thème (ii) (écoulement d'un cours d'eau) et résumé par des tableaux pour les cinq autres thèmes. Question 2 : les points imprimés somment à 23 (5+3+4+4+5+2), conformément à la page de garde ; « (Total = 23 marks) » est imprimé au bas de la question. Dans le sujet, le (f) précède l'indication « (2 marks) » placée au bas de la page.

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) Locate and describe the area where the field work was carried out. (5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
This answer depends on the candidate's own field work. A full-mark answer is built on the following plan, shown here for topic (ii), *stream channel flow characteristics*; the same plan serves the other five topics.

1. **Location (2 marks).** Name the place and the stream or site studied, its Region and Division, and its position relative to a known town or to the school (direction and distance in km); add latitude and longitude or a map grid reference. A small **sketch map** with title, north arrow, scale and key, showing the study stretch, the settlements and the roads, earns marks (marks are awarded for well annotated maps).
2. **Description (3 marks).** Describe the physical and human setting that matters for the topic: relief and slope of the basin (upper, middle or lower course), the rock or soil type, the climate and the season in which the work was done, the natural vegetation and the land use around the stream (farms, settlement, forest), and the length and number of sites of the study stretch (for example a stretch of about 100 m with six sampling sites placed at regular intervals).

*Do not invent a place: write about the area you actually visited.*

**Adapting the plan to the other topics.**

| Topic | What the description of the area must stress |
|---|---|
| (i) Rock and relief | Rock types and structure, slopes and landforms of the site, height above sea level |
| (iii) Vegetation characteristics | Climate, soils, altitude, human disturbance, type of vegetation zone |
| (iv) Traffic flow characteristics | The road or junction, its class (tarred or earth), the settlement it serves, land use around it |
| (v) Rural or urban land use | The settlement, its size and age, its functional zones or farming types, accessibility |
| (vi) Modern farm or cottage industry | The enterprise, its owner, the products, nearby market and inputs, transport links |

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) State the aim(s) and the hypothesis. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Aim (1 to 2 marks).** An aim states in one sentence what the study sets out to find out. For topic (ii): *to investigate how the characteristics of stream channel flow (width, depth, velocity and discharge) change from the upstream to the downstream end of the stream.*

**Hypothesis (1 to 2 marks).** A hypothesis is a testable statement. For topic (ii): *"Channel width, depth, velocity and discharge increase downstream."* It can be paired with a null hypothesis: *"There is no significant change in channel characteristics downstream."*

**The same logic for the other topics** (an aim begins with "to investigate", "to find out" or "to determine"; a hypothesis makes a clear statement of relationship that the data can accept or reject):

| Topic | Example hypothesis |
|---|---|
| (i) Rock and relief | Slope angle is steeper on the more resistant rock than on the less resistant rock |
| (iii) Vegetation | Plant species diversity and tree height decrease with increasing altitude (or with increasing human disturbance) |
| (iv) Traffic flow | Traffic volume is higher at the town centre than at the edge of the town, and peaks at rush hours |
| (v) Land use | Land use changes with distance from the town centre, with commerce at the centre and residential or farming use farther out |
| (vi) Modern farm or cottage industry | The location of the enterprise is explained by the nearness of the market, inputs, labour and transport |

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Outline the type of data and the tools needed for the investigation of the chosen topic. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Type of data (2 marks).**
- **Primary data** collected by the candidate in the field: for topic (ii) the width, depth, velocity, discharge, gradient and the size and roundness of the bed load, at each sampling site; photographs and field sketches.
- **Secondary data** from existing sources: topographical maps of the area, rainfall records, and earlier studies of the stream.

**Tools (2 marks).** For topic (ii): a tape measure (width), a metre rule or graduated stick (depth), a float such as an orange or a cork and a stopwatch, or a flow meter (velocity), a clinometer (slope), ranging poles, callipers or a ruler for pebbles, a notebook and pencils, a camera and a map of the area.

| Topic | Main data | Main tools |
|---|---|---|
| (i) Rock and relief | Rock type, dip, slope angles, height | Clinometer, ranging poles, tape, compass, hand lens, notebook |
| (iii) Vegetation | Species, cover, height, density | Quadrat, tape, identification key, notebook |
| (iv) Traffic flow | Number and type of vehicles per time | Tally sheet, stopwatch, notebook |
| (v) Land use | Use of each building or plot | Base map, questionnaire, colour code sheet |
| (vi) Farm or cottage industry | Inputs, output, labour, marketing | Interview schedule or questionnaire, camera |

questions.enonce_markdown: (d) Briefly describe how you used the tools on the field to obtain the required data in (c) above. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
State the procedure in the order carried out, with the **sampling method**, and give the precautions. For topic (ii), stream channel flow:

1. **Sampling.** Systematic sampling: six sites were chosen along the stream at regular intervals, from upstream to downstream, using a map and a tape measure; at each site a cross-section was fixed with two ranging poles on the banks.
2. **Width.** A tape was stretched across the surface of the water from bank to bank at right angles to the flow, and read to the nearest centimetre.
3. **Depth.** At regular intervals across the tape (for example every 20 cm or every 0.5 m) the depth was measured with a graduated stick held vertically on the bed; the readings give the cross-section and its area.
4. **Velocity.** A float was released upstream of a marked 10 m reach in the middle of the stream and timed with a stopwatch over the reach; the test was repeated at least three times and the mean taken; velocity = distance divided by time.
5. **Gradient and bed load.** A clinometer sighted between two ranging poles gave the slope; about 10 or 20 pebbles were picked at random on the bed and measured with callipers or a ruler.
6. **Recording and safety.** Every reading was written at once in a prepared table; the team worked in pairs, avoided deep or fast water and wore suitable footwear.

*For another topic, describe in the same way the use of your own tools (quadrat placement, tally of vehicles in successive 10-minute periods, questionnaire administration, and so on).*

questions.enonce_markdown: (e) How was your data processed and your results presented? (5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Processing (2 to 3 marks).** The raw data were entered in tables and summarised. For topic (ii): the **mean** of the repeated velocity readings at each site; the **cross-sectional area** $A$ (width multiplied by mean depth) and the **discharge**

$$
Q = A \times v
$$

with $Q$ in $\mathrm{m^3\,s^{-1}}$, $A$ in $\mathrm{m^2}$ and $v$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ (each site giving a value); the **mean pebble size** and a roundness index; and, where the hypothesis speaks of a relationship, a statistical test such as **Spearman's rank correlation coefficient**

$$
r_s = 1 - \dfrac{6\sum d^2}{n(n^2-1)}
$$

between distance downstream and width (or discharge), with $d$ the difference between the two ranks of each site and $n$ the number of sites.

**Presentation (2 to 3 marks).** Results were presented in a neat table, with **line or bar graphs** of width, depth, velocity and discharge plotted against distance downstream, **cross-section diagrams** of the channel at the sites, a **scatter graph** with a best-fit line, a **sketch map** of the sites, and **annotated photographs**; each graph is titled, with labelled axes, units and scale.

questions.enonce_markdown: (f) What conclusion was arrived at in relation to your hypothesis? (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
A conclusion must refer to the hypothesis, state whether it is **accepted, partly accepted or rejected**, and support the decision with evidence from the results. For topic (ii), a typical result, to be replaced by the candidate's own findings: *"The hypothesis that width, depth, velocity and discharge increase downstream was largely accepted: width, depth and discharge rose from site 1 to site 6 and Spearman's coefficient was strongly positive (close to +1), which is expected as tributaries add water and the channel enlarges. Velocity did not increase at every site because of local differences in bed roughness and channel shape, so that part of the hypothesis was only partly accepted."*

Add one limitation (a small number of sites, the season of the study, the accuracy of the float method) and, if asked, one recommendation. The marks are for linking the conclusion to the hypothesis and to the data.
